mechanism_narrative: A high federal funds rate indicates tight monetary conditions, which increases borrowing costs and reduces consumer and business spending, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of periods when FEDFUNDS is above 5%, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate signals labor market weakness, which may lead to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of periods when UNRATE increases by >0.2pp, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts indicates strong demand in the housing market, which may lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns in more than 30% of periods when HOUST increases, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production suggests supply chain disruptions or reduced economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of periods when INDPRO falls below 100, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in GDP growth combined with rising consumer prices indicates stagflation, which may lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns in more than 30% of periods when GDPC1 growth slows and CPIAUCSL rises, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A high federal funds rate in a monetary tightening cycle increases the cost of capital, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 5%, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: Strong payroll growth indicates a tight labor market, which may lead to wage inflation and subsequent monetary policy tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of periods when PAYEMS growth is strong, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in retail sales growth indicates weaker consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns in more than 30% of periods when RSAFS growth is below 3% YoY, this hypothesis is falsified.
